cohort: The study included 353 pregnancies in 273 women with rheumatic heart disease.
finding: Women with severe MS or poor NYHA status had worse pregnancy outcomes, including lower gestational age, lower birth weight, and higher perinatal and maternal mortality, while BMV improved outcomes when indicated.
mod_finding: Patients with RHD can undergo labor and vaginal delivery under vigilant monitoring.
birth_weight: Women with severe MS had lesser birth weight than those with mild-to-moderate MS; women with NYHA III-IV status had lesser birth weight.
gest_age: Women with severe MS had lesser gestational age at delivery than those with mild-to-moderate MS; women with NYHA III-IV status delivered at lesser gestational age.
